home.heroSubtitle: Full-stack monorepo application built with .NET 10 and React 19. Features a complete E-Commerce platform, Person Registration system with business-rule validation, Theoretical Q&A module, and an Admin Panel — all with full internationalization (EN/ES), Docker orchestration, and Swagger documentation.
home.featureEcommerceDesc: Product catalog with shopping cart, checkout flow, and category badges. Backed by a RESTful API with Accept-Language localization.
home.featureRegistrationDesc: Form with real-time validation enforcing business rules: alphanumeric IDs, no numbers in names, max 2 contacts per type.
home.featureQADesc: Complete React and .NET/SQL knowledge tests with answers. Fully translatable via i18n JSON locale files.
home.featureAdminDesc: Full CRUD management for Products and Categories with bilingual fields, Pexels image search integration, and duplicate validation.
home.archDesc: This application follows a clean monorepo structure with a Docker Compose orchestration layer. The backend exposes a RESTful API documented via Swagger/OpenAPI, while the frontend consumes it through typed fetch calls with Accept-Language headers for dynamic localization.
home.docSwaggerDesc: Interactive API documentation auto-generated from the .NET backend. Explore all endpoints, models, and try requests live.
home.docTypedocDesc: Static documentation generated from TypeScript source code, detailing all React components, contexts, and hooks.
home.docGherkinDesc: Behavior-Driven Development specifications describing all functional requirements in executable Gherkin syntax (.feature files).

qa.description: Implementation of React and .NET knowledge tests.

reactQuestions.q: 1. What is the error in this useEffect?
reactQuestions.a: Answer C: The dependency array should be []. (Option C is correct because props.value was passed directly instead of [props.value]).

reactQuestions.q: 2. What happens with this React state?
reactQuestions.a: Answer B: Both calls use the same previous value, so it only increments once. (State is queued without callback prev => prev + 1).

reactQuestions.q: 3. Why doesn't this useContext update child components?
reactQuestions.a: Answer C: The cart state is not tied to useState, so changes aren't detected.

reactQuestions.q: 4. What is the problem with this useEffect?
reactQuestions.a: Answer D: If fetchData depends on props or state, it should be in the dependency array.

reactQuestions.q: 5. What happens with the following useReducer?
reactQuestions.a: Answer B: The state is being mutated directly; it should return a new copy.

reactQuestions.q: 6. Why doesn't the button onClick={handleClick()} work?
reactQuestions.a: Answer B: The handleClick() function executes immediately upon rendering.

reactQuestions.q: 7. What is wrong with const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState();?
reactQuestions.a: Answer C: The input might show undefined; it's recommended to initialize with ''.

reactQuestions.q: 8. What problem is caused by setCounter(counter + 1) inside a useEffect depending on [counter]?
reactQuestions.a: Answer B: This can cause an infinite loop of updates.

reactQuestions.q: 9. What is a common risk when using nested useContext?
reactQuestions.a: Answer C: If any context lacks a parent Provider, it will return undefined.

reactQuestions.q: 10. What is a risk when updating objects with useState using setUser(user);?
reactQuestions.a: Answer A: If user's reference doesn't change, React won't re-render.
